title: bug: the ps1 hot reload nests a new wrapper per script change, so seats accumulate blocked PowerShell parents (5.5 GB after one night)
description: Measured by the governor on 2026-09-19 06:50Z. df42861 made the ps1 self-restart hand over with the call operator so the reloaded wrapper keeps its console, which fixed the duplicate-seat bug from Start-Process. The cost is that every moe-agent.ps1 change leaves the old wrapper blocked on its child forever, one extra process per seat per change. After one night of landings that touched the launchers, this project had 45 seat wrappers alive, 6.2 GB working set, of which 38 were blocked reload parents holding 5.5 GB. Depth per seat was 5 to 8. Nothing bounds it inside a session, and it cannot be cleaned up piecemeal: killing an intermediate parent unblocks ITS parent, which resumes the claim loop while the innermost wrapper is still live, which is the duplicate-seat failure df42861 fixed. Today the only safe cleanup is stopping a seat's whole process tree and relaunching it. Wanted: a hand-over that does not nest, for example a thin supervisor that launches the agent script once per iteration so a reload is just the next iteration reading the new file, while the console and the one-loop-per-seat guarantee are preserved. The sh twin exec()s in place and has no such growth, so this is a ps1-only defect; keep the twins behaviourally equal.
definitionOfDone: A moe-agent.ps1 hot reload leaves no blocked parent: after N script changes a seat still has exactly one wrapper process, proven by a postflight arm that counts wrapper processes across two reloads
The reload still keeps the seat's console and never produces a second claim loop for the same worker id (the df42861 regression stays covered)
parity-check.{sh,ps1} pass and the sh twin's exec hand-over is unchanged

implementationPlan.description:
RED FIRST: a hot-reload arm in scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, the only harness that runs the ps1 wrapper. This task waits on task-d1441364, which edits the same two files, so find code by function name.

Arm 'hot reload keeps one wrapper process':
1. Copy the repo's scripts/ into a temp root, plus docs/roles if the wrapper loads role docs from there, so the arm edits a COPY and never the live launcher.
2. Run the copied moe-agent.ps1 with -Loop -PollInterval 1 against the existing fake proxy, with FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle and MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1, via Start-Process -PassThru with redirected output.
3. Wait for the first logged claim_next_task.
4. Twice: append a comment line ('# reload N') to the copied moe-agent.ps1. Wait until the fake's deregister.log shows a 'wrapper_restart' deregister AND a later claim is logged. Then count wrapper processes: Win32_Process whose CommandLine contains the copied script path and whose executable is pwsh or powershell. The heartbeat job is disabled, so it is not counted.
5. Stop the whole tree (taskkill /T /F), as the loop arms do.

Assertions:
(a) exactly 2 wrapper_restart deregisters;
(b) exactly 1 wrapper process after EACH reload;
(c) every claim_next_task across both reloads carries ONE runner identity (processStartedAt/host) — one process, one claim loop;
(d) at least one claim after the second reload, so the seat keeps working.

On today's wrapper it must FAIL: each reload spawns `& $exe @args` and blocks, so (b) sees 2 and then 3 processes, and (c) sees three identities. Run it on pwsh 7 AND PS 5.1, launched from PowerShell, never from Git Bash, and paste both failures. The sh harness gets no arm: the sh twin execs in place and is unchanged by this task.

PROCESS-GLOBAL STATE that a same-process rerun would otherwise accumulate or freeze. Both are in scripts/moe-agent.ps1.

1. PowerShell.Exiting subscriber (Register-EngineEvent near the top). Each run would add another subscriber bound to its own, now dead, script scope. Before registering, run `Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier PowerShell.Exiting -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` (this process has no other subscriber to it), then register as today. Exactly one handler, the current run's, deregisters the current worker on window close.
2. Add-Type of MoeFrozenGateProcess. A compiled type lives as long as the process, so after an in-process reload a CHANGED C# definition would silently keep the old code.
   - Name the class after its definition: keep a placeholder in $script:MoeGateProcessDefinition, and set $script:MoeGateTypeName = 'MoeFrozenGateProcess' + the first 12 hex digits of SHA256(the definition text).
   - Substitute that name into the definition, and have Initialize-MoeGateProcess test `$script:MoeGateTypeName -as [type]` before calling Add-Type.
   - Create instances with New-Object -TypeName $script:MoeGateTypeName -ArgumentList @(...).
   An unchanged definition reuses the loaded type. A changed one compiles a new name.
3. Confirm everything else is per run and needs nothing: env vars are set each run and cleaned in the finally; the heartbeat Start-Job is stopped in the finally; the $global:OutputEncoding swap is restored inside Invoke-MoeRpc; TreatControlCAsInput=$false is idempotent. Say so in the step note.

VERIFY, sequentially, launched from PowerShell, with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=400.
1. The new arm is green on pwsh 7 and on PS 5.1 (powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, or isolate the arm while iterating).
2. The full postflight.ps1 on pwsh 7 and PS 5.1. The frozen suite's gate arms (interrupt-int, integrity-batch, exit-tail and the rest) create the renamed gate type, and the loop arms stop the wrapper tree, so they exercise both halves.
3. node --test scripts/tests/agent-runtime.test.mjs scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs. Both spawn the ps1 wrapper on Windows.
4. pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/importee-guard.ps1 and powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/importee-guard.ps1.
5. Parity: bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh, pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1, powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1. Also confirm git diff shows no change to scripts/moe-agent.sh.
6. For complete_task, the verification is the full postflight.ps1 on pwsh, with its PASS line as outputTail.

SELF-REVIEW, posted as a task comment:
1. Can two claim loops ever exist for one seat? One process means one supervisor; after the break, the previous pass has returned before the next `&`.
2. What does Ctrl+C do inside the rerun boundary? The pipeline stops, the finally cleans up, and there is no reload.
3. Could a stale PowerShell.Exiting handler deregister the wrong run, or none? Exactly one subscriber exists, the current run's.
4. Does a changed gate C# definition take effect after a reload (new type name), and does an unchanged one avoid a second Add-Type?
5. Is every exit code the same as before, for normal exit, -Loop -NoLoop and single-shot?
6. PS 5.1 specifics: splatting a switch left bound as $false (-Interactive:$false), and $LASTEXITCODE after a script `exit`.
7. Is the sh twin untouched? git diff --stat shows only the two planned paths.

Related memories for the reviewer: moes-ps1-hotreload-detach (df42861) and moes-duplicate-seat-wrapper.

reopenReason: Human approved: ps1 hot-reload nesting, 45 wrappers / 5.5 GB of blocked parents measured 2026-09-19 06:50Z.

comments.author: governor-39911495
comments.content: Governor data point for the implementer (2026-09-19 09:05Z): the growth is driven by edits, not only by landings. Idle seats poll every 30 s, and each poll checks the moe-agent.ps1 hash, so every SAVE a worker makes to the repo copy while developing reloads every idle ps1 seat, one nesting level each. Between 09:02:58Z and 09:04:48Z, while task-d1441364's worker was editing moe-agent.ps1, qa-7100be29, qa-5e66a826 and qa-9a371c33 each reloaded (wrapper_restart), taking this project from 45 to 48 seat wrappers with 41 blocked parents. Free RAM went from 22.6 GB to 19.0 GB over the morning. Two consequences for the plan: (1) once the hand-over stops nesting, a reload storm during development costs nothing, so fix the nesting first; (2) if the design keeps any per-reload cost, reload only when the hash has been stable for a short window, so a burst of saves costs one reload, not N. Keep the one-loop-per-seat and keep-the-console guarantees from df42861.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A separate thin supervisor file with the body in moe-agent-core.ps1: rejected. It changes what the JetBrains/VS Code bundles, parity-check, the harnesses and the docs point at, for the same effect as the in-file prologue.
- Start-Process -NoNewWindow followed by the parent exiting: rejected. The launching shell returns to its prompt while the child writes to the same console, which is the dead-looking-seat confusion df42861 fixed.
- Recursing into the script in-process at the bottom (`& $PSCommandPath` without a loop): rejected. It still nests call frames and scopes per reload, and it would reach PowerShell's call-depth limit over a long run.
- Keeping the child-process relaunch and reaping old parents: rejected. Killing an intermediate parent resumes ITS parent's loop, which is the duplicate-seat failure.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Today's hand-over is at the bottom of moe-agent.ps1: after the outer finally, `& $moeRelaunchExe @moeRelaunchArgs; exit $LASTEXITCODE`. The parent blocks for the child's whole life.
- The restart check sits at the top of each loop iteration: hash change, then Invoke-MoeDeregister 'wrapper_restart', then break.
- Process-global side effects in the body:
  - Register-EngineEvent PowerShell.Exiting near the top: accumulates on every run.
  - Add-Type of MoeFrozenGateProcess (guarded by -as [type], used through New-Object by name): would freeze old C# after a reload.
  - Everything else is per run.
- The param block has no ValueFromRemainingArguments, so @PSBoundParameters forwards everything.
- No test covers the self-restart today (task-e92b2cb3 is in BACKLOG).
- The runner identity is <pid>@<start token>, so an in-process reload keeps it, which is better for reattach than a new child PID.
planningNotes.risks:
- The arm must edit a COPY of the wrapper, never the live scripts/moe-agent.ps1: repo-launched seats hot-reload on every edit of that file (mem:moes-installed-plugin-staleness).
- Process counting under fleet load: match on the unique copied script path and on the pwsh or powershell executable only, and poll with a deadline rather than a fixed sleep.
- PS 5.1 differences: the $global variable scoping, `exit` inside a script invoked with &, and splatting SwitchParameter values. Test both engines.
- A reload that changes the param() block can fail to bind the old parameters; that is the same outcome as today's child relaunch, and the catch keeps it a clear stop.
- dependsOn task-d1441364, which edits the same two files. Re-check git status before editing.
